name: All Domains
title: CAFS Executive Revision Brief
subtitle: A single-page overview of what you should be able to explain without notes.
items: Domain 1 Fraud Risk Management 40%; Domain 2 Detection & Analytics 30%; Domain 3 Investigations 30%.
Pressure/incentive + opportunity + rationalization. Weak controls create opportunity.
First: own identity; second: knowingly collaborates; third: unrelated outsider. The supplied guide places synthetic fraud under first-party.
US Regulation E: unauthorized EFT error handling. UK PSR: unauthorized payments. UK APP reimbursement: deceived sender authorizes payment.
1st operates prevention/detection/response; 2nd oversees policy, compliance and appetite; 3rd independently assures.
Identify fraud types → inherent risk → assess controls → residual risk → prioritize against appetite → monitor.
Document risks → assess impact/likelihood → evaluate controls → develop actions.
Preventive: segregation/four eyes/MFA. Detective: monitoring/anomalies/alerts. Controls must be tested and tuned.
Onboarding → active relationship and changes → detect/contain/response → customer exit → feedback.
APP: deceived victim initiates the payment. ATO: attacker takes unauthorized control of an existing account.
Combine transactions + CRM + device/IP + login/password events + calls/location + external intelligence.
Extract sources → transform/clean/standardize → load; mining finds patterns, matching links records.
Supervised = labeled historical fraud; unsupervised = unlabeled pattern/anomaly discovery. Combine with rules.
TP/(TP+FP): of cases flagged as fraud, how many were genuine?
TP/(TP+FN): of all actual fraud, how many did the model catch?
F1 = 2PR/(P+R); specificity = TN/(TN+FP). Accuracy can mislead when fraud is rare.
Define → gather/clean → engineer features → select → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor/refine.
Link = connections; centrality = key hubs; closeness = distance; clustering = groups.
Policy/SLA → triage → preserve evidence / protect victim → investigate productive alerts → reasoned decision.
Case creation → initial review → stakeholder notification → investigation → conclusion and sharing.
Relevance, lawful collection, authenticity, preservation, chain of custody, corroboration, audit trail.
Use empathy, avoid blame, explain simply, do not treat victim reluctance as proof of dishonesty.
Typology is HOW scheme operated; RCA is WHY controls failed or allowed it to persist.
Sufficient evidence → documented rationale → loss/recovery/reporting/account action → feedback to controls.

name: Domain 1
title: Fraud Risk Management
subtitle: From fraud definition and governance to response, remediation and assurance.
items: Fraud is intentional criminal deception for an unjust or illegal advantage; ordinary error lacks fraudulent intent.
Pressure (e.g., debt); opportunity (weak control); rationalization (“I will pay it back”).
Insider/occupational/employee fraud versus outsiders such as vendor, customer, hacker or criminal group.
First = own identity; second = knowing collaboration; third = unrelated perpetrator. Synthetic first-party in supplied taxonomy.
First operates; second policies/oversight/compliance; third independent assurance and audit. Ownership can vary by firm.
Risk taxonomy, appetite, governance, reporting, training, whistleblowing, assessments and control effectiveness.
Inherent exposure before controls; residual exposure after controls. Risk-based focus on severity, likelihood and mitigation.
Enterprise-wide + line-of-business; assess internal/external/seasonal/products/channels and collusion; refresh as threats evolve.
Document risks; Assess impact and likelihood; Evaluate control strength; Develop action plan.
Customer, Jurisdiction, Product, Channel. Each changes fraud exposures and detection needs.
Identity fraud; bust-out; synthetic identities; coerced or mule-based origination.
Genuine identity, initially performs normally, then raises available credit and defaults deliberately.
Segregation of duties, four-eyes checks, limited approvals, identity verification, KYE/KYV, MFA and training.
Transaction monitoring, velocity rules, anomaly scoring, device intelligence, staff access patterns and alerts.
Customer onboarding → ongoing account relationship → changes/transactions → response and exit, with learning loop.
Acceptable fraud risk/loss threshold guides investment, prioritization, thresholds and escalation.
Define purpose, scope, roles, controls, investigation, escalation, whistleblowing, remediation, review and board oversight.
Begin with risk-based business use case, consult stakeholders, compare vendor/in-house capability, ROI and control gaps.
Fraud response plan identifies triggers, contacts, responsibilities, evidence handling, containment, communication, reporting.
Depending on payment type: chargeback, ACH/wire recall or reversal, SWIFT recall, interbank coordination, indemnity.
Suspicious activity reporting is jurisdiction-sensitive; investigation facts and internal escalation support FIU reporting.
Investigate root causes; tune controls; track losses, false positives, friction, recovery, fraud bps and ROI.
In the guide’s smishing bank scenario, best response was re-evaluate fraud budget from updated risk assessment.

name: Domain 2
title: Fraud Detection & Analytics
subtitle: Data → techniques → models → metrics → operational deployment.
items: Use customer, employee, operational and transaction data to find anomalous patterns and prevent/detect fraud.
Criminals may gather credentials through a less secure channel, then execute on a more secure channel.
Card-not-present: remote misuse; BIN attack: many rapid card tests; APP: manipulated sender approves payment.
Know normal customers/devices/hours/payees before flagging deviations; combine multiple indicators.
Transactions/history; CRM and demographics; nonmonetary events; device identifiers/IP.
Payment networks/processors, credit agencies, fraud-sharing platforms and risk engines.
Structured = fields, dates, amounts; unstructured = documents, photos, recordings.
Extract → Transform → Load. Clean duplicates, missing values and inconsistent formats before analysis.
Feature engineering creates variables; normalization scales values; encoding turns categories into numeric inputs.
Mining finds hidden patterns; matching cross-references entities/attributes to reveal links or inconsistencies.
Unusual user behavior + unusual organization behavior + known fraud patterns.
Trend analysis, clustering, statistical outliers, descriptive/predictive analytics, SNA and rules.
Rules give transparent thresholds; ML combines many features. Neither should automatically replace the other.
Link, centrality, closeness and clustering; suitable for shared devices, payees, addresses and fraud rings.
Supervised learns from labeled fraud/genuine activity; unsupervised looks for structure or anomalies without labels.
Define → data → features → select → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor/refine.
TP caught fraud; FP innocent flagged; FN missed fraud; TN legitimate cleared.
TP/(TP+FP): accuracy among flagged transactions; low precision means many false positives.
TP/(TP+FN): proportion of true fraud caught; low recall means many missed fraud cases.
F1 harmonizes precision and recall. Specificity = TN/(TN+FP), correct negatives among actual negatives.
Fraud is rare; a “predict all genuine” model can appear accurate while catching no fraud.
Training success can fail on new data; monitor model degradation and update labels, thresholds and models.
Use separate train/validation/test data; back-testing, out-of-sample checks, controlled rollout, rollback and human oversight.

name: Domain 3
title: Fraud Investigations
subtitle: From alert triage and typologies through defensible evidence and closure.
items: Prevention is proactive; detection finds fraud in progress or after the event. Both are essential.
Detect, investigate, prevent, report and educate/train.
Curiosity; analytical thinking; healthy skepticism; alertness to red flags.
Check policy and SLA → triage → interim protection → productive or nonproductive decision → investigator.
Case creation → initial review → stakeholder notification → investigation → conclusion/intelligence sharing.
Risk-based, monetary-loss based and customer-impact based.
APP victim authorizes after deception; ATO offender gains unauthorized account access/control.
Phishing email; vishing voice; smishing SMS; spear phishing tailored; BEC executive or business impersonation.
Ponzi = returns using later investors; pyramid = compensation mainly for recruiting; pig butchering = relationship investment scam.
Unwitting; witting/willfully blind; complicit. Investigate evidence before deciding victim versus participant.
Asset misappropriation; fraudulent financial statements; bribery and corruption; phantom vendors and ghost staff.
Counterfeit is fabricated; forged is genuine but materially altered. Examine authenticity and provenance.
Profile mismatches, changed contacts, unusual activity, multiple accounts sharing identity/device or common payee.
Collect lawfully → preserve originals → track custody → independently corroborate → document decisions.
Assess public-record reliability and privacy requirements; keep search notes and evidentiary limitations.
Identify transaction path, messages and receiving institutions; coordinate rapid protective action and recalls.
Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication; a messaging network, not itself funds settlement.
Prepare open questions; avoid leading witnesses; distinguish Reid and PEACE methods and record accurate statements.
Often victim/whistleblower → neutral witnesses → associated witnesses → suspect, depending on case needs.
Ask why the control failed, not merely which fraud method occurred; connect action owner and remediation.
Use empathetic nonjudgmental language; protect victims and avoid pressuring those still influenced by a scammer.
Chronology, scope, sources, evidence, limitations, findings, decision rationale, losses and recommended actions.
An alert or isolated red flag does not establish fraud; closure must rest on corroborated and appropriate evidence.
Analytics + investigation + risk management → root cause, rule tuning, awareness and control enhancements.
